subject.title: Auto-apply safe doctor fixes on gateway start

question: Should Gateway startup ever persist doctor repairs automatically, and if so which repair classes are safe enough for unattended startup execution?
rationale: This changes a security-, provider-, and channel-sensitive startup boundary where current code and docs deliberately validate-and-guide instead of mutating persistent config.

options.title: Keep Startup Read-Only
options.body: Leave Gateway startup as validate-and-guide, fix narrower doctor bugs separately, and keep persistent config repair operator-initiated.

options.title: Add Opt-In Safe Startup Repair
options.body: Define an allowlisted repair subset with backups, changed-path logs, and upgrade tests before exposing a named opt-in setting or setup choice.

options.title: Auto-Apply By Default
options.body: Allow default startup self-healing only after maintainers accept compatibility and security risk with broad release proof.

recommendation.title: Keep Startup Read-Only
recommendation.body: Leave Gateway startup as validate-and-guide, fix narrower doctor bugs separately, and keep persistent config repair operator-initiated.

likelyOwner.reason: The remaining choice is the product/security policy for doctor-owned config repair during Gateway startup, and Peter has the strongest recent history on doctor repair orchestration and related documentation.
